home.sub: Roatán, Utila, Guanaja and Cayos Cochinos are surrounded by coral reefs. Explore their seafloor in 3D, learn what keeps a reef healthy, and see from satellite data when the sea gets too hot.
home.mapLabel: Map of the Bay Islands with the latest heat stress
home.cardsLead: Average of the 5 km cells around each island. Degree heating weeks (°C-weeks) add up the extra heat of the last 12 weeks.
home.stripesTitle: Forty years of heat, island by island
home.stripesLead: Each stripe is one year, colored by the highest heat stress that island had.
home.caveat: These are satellite measurements of the ocean surface in 5 km cells: a regional signal, not a measurement on any one reef.
alert.building.desc: Heat building up: risk of possible bleaching.
alert.a2.desc: Risk of reef-wide bleaching with death of heat-sensitive corals.
alert.a4.desc: Risk of severe, multi-species mortality (over 50% of corals).
alert.a5.desc: Risk of near-complete mortality (over 80% of corals).
heat.title: Heat stress, *island by island*
heat.lead: NOAA publishes ocean heat for the whole planet, but not island by island. Here we compute it for each island group from the daily 5 km satellite grid.
heat.chartLead: Heat built up day by day around each island. The shaded band is bleaching season (August to October).
scene.hover: Move the cursor over the island to see its data.
scene.exaggeration: Relief exaggerated ×4; depths beyond 40 m compressed.
scene.modelNote: Satellite-based model; not a navigation chart.
scene.depthModel: Shallow depths estimated from reef zones (satellite bathymetry pending).
scene.heatNote: Each square is one 5 km satellite cell: a regional signal, not a measurement on a reef.
scene.noWebgl: Your device can't show 3D. You can see each island's data under Heat stress.
scene.modelSoon: 3D model of a real coral: coming soon.
learn.title: Learn about *reefs*
learn.lead: Short explanations to understand what the maps and charts show.
about.title: Data *& credits*
about.lead: ReefQuest is free and nonprofit. Everything you see comes from open data, processed by us and stored on this site. This is how it works and where its limits are.
about.caveatsTitle: What these data *can and can't* tell you
nowebgl.title: Your device can't show 3D
nowebgl.body: You can still use the map and the heat-stress charts.
footer.made: Made in Honduras for the islands' schools, communities and divers.
footer.free: Free, nonprofit and built on open data.
scene.hint: Drag to move, scroll or pinch to zoom, and hold Shift while dragging (or drag with two fingers) to rotate. Tap the dots to read their stories.
boat.title: Research vessel R/V Arrecife
boat.heading: Heading
boat.mission: Mission: make a CTD cast over every habitat in this zone.
boat.missionDone: Mission complete: you logged every habitat in the zone.
boat.aground: Shallow water! Back up or tap deeper water.
boat.empty: No samples yet. Sail over the reef and take one.
boat.illustrative: Corals, sponges, fish and vegetation are illustrative, placed by the maps; they don't represent real species. Large animals and wrecks: what the sources document at each place, with illustrative shape and number.
home.title: Meet the reef *around our islands.*
home.fig1Title: Latest heat stress across the Bay Islands
home.fig1Sub: Degree heating weeks in 5 km satellite cells, {date}.
home.fig1Caption: Each square is one 5 km cell of NOAA's product, colored by the heat built up over the last 12 weeks; from 4 °C-weeks, bleaching is expected. Lines are depth contours. Tap an island to open it.
home.fig1Source: Source: NOAA Coral Reef Watch v3.1 (5 km). Depth and mainland coast: GEBCO 2023. Islands: © OpenStreetMap contributors. Chart: ReefQuest.
home.tableNote: The dotted line in the small charts marks 4 °C-weeks (Alert 1).
heat.source: Source: NOAA Coral Reef Watch v3.1 (5 km), data through {date}. Island averages: ReefQuest.
heat.recordLead: The three years with the most heat stress on each island. Tap a row to show it in the figure.
heat.scaleLead: NOAA extended the scale in 2023 with three new levels for extreme events.
scene.attribution: Data: NOAA CRW · Allen Coral Atlas · Copernicus DEM · GEBCO 2023 · © OpenStreetMap
scene.timebarKey: Each stripe is one year, colored by its heat peak. Tap one to jump to that year.
scene.timebarKeyShort: Each stripe is a year, by its heat peak. Tap one.
boat.zonesLead: Sail a research vessel over the reef, map the seafloor and take samples.
scene.layer.habitat.what: Colors of the Allen Coral Atlas satellite classification, instead of the natural view.
scene.layer.heat.what: Heat built up in NOAA 5 km cells, on the date below.
scene.layer.contours.what: Depth every 5 m over the reef; every 200 m offshore.
scene.aboutData: About the data and its limits
scene.guide1: Move the map. Click and drag to pan, scroll the wheel to zoom, and hold Shift while you drag to turn it.
scene.guide2: Click a boat. Each little boat on the water is a place with a story; from there you can set out to sea.
scene.guide3: Play the heat. Press ▶ on the timeline at the bottom: the sea turns red and purple when the heat is enough to bleach corals.
scene.guide4: Change the map. In “Map layers” on the left, turn on the habitat map to see sand, seagrass and reef.
scene.guideIntro: A 3D model of the island, its reefs and the heat they have been through.
scene.guide1Touch: Move the map. Drag with one finger, pinch to zoom, and twist two fingers to turn it.
scene.guide2Touch: Tap a boat. Each little boat on the water is a place with a story; from there you can set out to sea.
scene.guide4Phone: Change the map. Tap “Layers” in the bottom bar and turn on the habitat map to see sand, seagrass and reef.
scene.mouse.title: Mouse controls
home.reliefCredit: Seafloor relief: GEBCO 2023 depth contours, 20 to 3,000 m.
boat.bleachNote: Corals are shown bleached because on {date} this area had built up {dhw} °C-weeks of heat. This illustrates NOAA's thresholds; it is not an observation of the site.
home.panelHint: Each stripe is one year, {a}–{b}. Darker and purple: more heat.
isles.title: Explore the islands *in 3D*
isles.lead: Pick an island to explore its relief, its reef and the sea's heat day by day, or board the research boat.
isles.note: Previews of the real relief and depth (Copernicus DEM, Allen Coral Atlas, GEBCO), with height exaggerated. They are a model, not a navigation chart.

hub.lead: Ocean heat island by island since 1985, and short lessons to understand what the maps show.
support.title: The people *protecting the reef*
support.lead: These organizations work for the reefs of the Bay Islands. You can support them with a donation or as a volunteer; each one explains how on its own site.
support.allLead: Outside organizations that fund and support the local ones.
support.note: It is not affiliated with these organizations, receives nothing from them and handles no donations for them: the links go to their own sites. The information comes from those sites, read on {date}. Before donating, confirm the details with the organization.
support.missing: Only organizations that work for the reef and have a website we could read are listed. There may be others.

boat.tapHint: Tap the water to sail there
mission.whale-shark.near: On course. Go in under 3 knots and look for the birds.
mission.whale-shark.far: Contact zone: under 3 knots, and stay out of the white water.
mission.whale-shark.watch: That's it, slowly. Hold still and wait.
mission.whale-shark.logged: You saw it! Hold still and press “Underwater”: it comes to you.
mission.whale-shark.close: Open the camera and photograph the whale shark.
mission.whale-shark.dived: It dived. Move off and come back slowly.
mission.turtles.above: Turtles swim around here. Press “Underwater” and wait for them.
mission.turtles.below: Hold still: they come over. Open the camera and photograph one.
mission.reef-sharks.above: The sharks are below, over the sand. Press “Underwater”.
mission.reef-sharks.below: Hold still: they circle you. Open the camera and photograph one.
mission.wreck.above: The wreck is right below. Press “Underwater”.
mission.wreck.below: Follow the hull and photograph the wreck.
mission.done: Photo in the logbook. Mission complete!
shot.hint: Under the water, open the camera at the marked places and frame what there is to find. Each photo completes a mission.
scene.guide3Phone: Play the heat. Press ▶ in “Heat”, the panel above the bottom bar: the sea turns red and purple when the heat is enough to bleach corals.
boat.edge: Edge of the survey area. Turn back.
